2. M.F.A. No.7662/2016 is filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, Bengaluru (KSRTC), and M.F.A. Crob. No.141/2018 is filed by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 11.05.2016 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru,

sentences.text: One C.N. Mansoor Pasha, aged 19 years, met with an accident on 09.08.2013 and died.
His parents and unmarried sister filed a claim application claiming compensation of Rs.10,10,000/-.
The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted Rs.8,51,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the deposit.

4. Aggrieved by the said order, the KSRTC has preferred M.F.A. No.7662/2016 contending that the negligence assessed by the Tribunal, so also the income taken by the Tribunal and also the amounts awarded under all the heads are excessive and requested for reduction in the compensation.

The NC: 2025:KHC:34929 HC-KAR claimants have preferred M.F.A. Crob. No.141/2018 mainly contending that the loss of dependency assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and hence sought for enhancement in the compensation.
5. It is stated that C. N. Mansoor Pasha was aged 19 years and he was doing radium cutting work and earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
But, no evidence is adduced to prove his income.

As the deceased met with an accident on 09.08.2013, his income is to be taken as Rs.8,000/- per month instead of Rs.7,500/- per month as per guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority and the multiplier to be taken is 18.
The total annual income, thus, comes to Rs.17,28,000/-.

The deceased is entitled for 40%
towards future prospects as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, after adding 40% towards future prospects, the amount would come to Rs.24,19,200/- (17,28,000+40%).

As the deceased was unmarried, 50% to be deducted towards personal expenses as per the judgment in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC:
2025:KHC:34929 HC-KAR Transport Corporation2.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.12,09,600/- (24,19,200x50%).
6.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, by reiterating the comprehensive interpretation of 'consortium' given in the authority of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others3, and in the authority between United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others4, fortified that the amounts for loss of consortium shall be awarded to the children who lose the care and protection of their parents as 'parental consortium' and to the parents as, 'filial consortium' for the loss of their grown-up children, to compensate their agony, love and affection, care and companionship of deceased children.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, it is just and reasonable to award towards filial consortium of Rs.80,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- each to petitioner-claimant Nos.1 and 2).
The 3rd petitioner-claimant is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and she is entitled for the said amount.
The (2009) 6 SCC 121 (2018) 18 SCC 130 (2020) 9 SCC 644 NC: 2025:KHC:34929 HC-KAR claimants are also entitled for Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the KSRTC that the rate of interest awarded on the compensation by the Tribunal is also on the higher side.
In view of the submission made by the learned counsel, this Court finds it just and reasonable to reduce the interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% per annum to 6% per annum.

8. It is further contended by the learned counsel for the KSRTC that the amount of Rs.50,000/- has been paid to the claimants for funeral expenses and hence, requested for the said amount to be deducted from the compensation awarded by this Court.

Therefore, by deducting Rs.50,000/- from Rs.13,59,600/-, the total compensation comes to Rs.13,09,600/-.(Thirteen Lakhs Nine Thousand and Six Hundred only)
9.
As the 3rd petitioner-claimant (sister of the deceased) might have married, she entitled for Rs.40,000/- and she is permitted to withdraw the said amount.

Further, this Court NC:
2025:KHC:34929 HC-KAR finds it reasonable to apportion the balance amount equally among 1st and 2nd claimant, who are parents of the deceased, and they are permitted to withdraw the entire amount on such deposit.
10. The claimants are entitled for the compensation of Rs.13,09,600/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.8,51,000/-/- awarded by the Tribunal.

11. The claimants filed objections to I.A. No.2/2016 filed by KSRTC, contending that, initially,
M.F.A. No.3235 of 2017 was filed by one Mujasir Pasha @ Majakeer Pasha @ Mudaseer Syed for enhancement, against the award in MVC 362 of 2013 and the said appeal was allowed on 29.01.2020 and the KSRTC accepted the liability, and thus now they cannot deny the liability.
